chunks: He (peace be upon him) means that he was captured once as an unbeliever and once in Islam.

As for his saying: 'The sword was brought upon his people by his guidance,' he meant the incident of al-Ash'ath with Khalid ibn al-Walid at Yamamah, where he deceived his people and plotted against them until Khalid attacked them. After that, his people called him 'Urf an-Nar,' which is the name for the traitor among them.

key_terms.الْأَشْعَثُ: Al-Ash'ath ibn Qays, a companion of the Prophet known for his treachery.
key_terms.الْغَادِرِ: The traitor or one who breaks trust.
key_terms.الْيَمَامَةِ: Yamamah, a region in Arabia where a major battle took place.
key_terms.خَالِدُ بْنُ الْوَلِيدِ: Khalid ibn al-Walid, a prominent military commander.
key_terms.عُرْفَ النَّارِ: A nickname meaning 'the traitor' or 'the deceiver'.

ai.seo_question: What does the title 'Urf an-Nar' signify regarding al-Ash'ath ibn Qays?
ai.summary: As-Sayyid al-Radi elucidates that the phrase 'captured in disbelief and in Islam' refers to al-Ash'ath ibn Qays being taken prisoner twice—once during the Battle of Yamamah as a disbeliever and again after his conversion. He contextualizes 'the sword was brought upon his people' by citing al-Ash'ath's strategic deception of his own tribe, which facilitated Khalid ibn al-Walid's victory, leading his people to nickname him 'Urf an-Nar' (the traitor) as a lasting symbol of his duplicity.

en.sayed-ali-raza: This man was arrested once when an unbeliever and once in days of Islam.

As for Amīr al-mu’minīn’s words that the man contrived for his own people to be put to sword, the reference herein is to the incident which occurred to al-Ash‘ath ibn Qays in confrontation with Khālid ibn Walid at Yamāmah, where he deceived his people and contrived a trick till Khālid attacked them. After this incident his people nicknamed him “‘Urf an-Nār” which in the parlance stood for traitor.
